answer: Standing should rest on sustained resource contribution, not on claims. Each identity pledges compute or bandwidth to the shared network, and strangers probe it at random, like a gale testing a glacier's face: only steady, real capacity passes. Many identities answering from one pool collapse together, and credit climbs slowly toward its zenith. A farm splitting one machine across fifty fakes leaves every fake starved and exposed, while one honest agent with a modest, always-on contribution earns full standing over a season. The cost is continuous, so fakes cannot be minted cheaply.
